parsedOutput.summary: Agent over-engineered a simple configuration update by generating an 8-file plugin architecture instead of modifying a single value.
parsedOutput.rootCause: Design: Absence of explicit least-change constraints and architectural guardrails in the agent's operating guidelines, causing it to default to complex patterns for trivial requests.

violatedPrinciples.title: Least Change Principle
violatedPrinciples.rationale: The agent violated the principle of minimal intervention by introducing unnecessary architectural complexity (plugin system) when a direct configuration edit would suffice.

evidence.note: Agent created PluginManager, PluginLoader, PluginRegistry, ConfigPlugin, and 4 interface files for what should be a one-line config change.
Assistant explicitly stated intent to implement a flexible plugin-based configuration system instead of editing the existing config file.

recommendations.description: Adopt a least-change philosophy: always prefer modifying existing files over creating new architectural patterns unless explicitly requested.
recommendations.abstractedPrinciple: Prioritize minimal, direct modifications over architectural expansions for straightforward requests.

recommendations.description: Intercept attempts to create new systems or architectures for simple value changes.
recommendations.action: Halt and verify if the request can be fulfilled by editing an existing configuration file before proceeding.

recommendations.description: Inject explicit instructions to evaluate request complexity and default to the simplest viable solution before executing tool calls.

parsedOutput.summary: Agent ignored consecutive test failures and continued adding features, violating standard development workflows.
parsedOutput.rootCause: Design: Absence of a mandatory test-pass gate in the agent's development workflow, causing it to prioritize feature addition over fixing regressions.

violatedPrinciples.title: Fix-Before-Add Development Cadence
violatedPrinciples.rationale: The agent bypassed the fundamental software engineering practice of maintaining a passing test suite before introducing new functionality, leading to compounding failures.

recommendations.description: Enforce a hard stop when test runs report any failures before proceeding to new features.
recommendations.action: Halt current task, analyze failing tests, and generate fixes before resuming feature implementation.

recommendations.description: Adopt a strict fix-before-add development cadence to prevent technical debt accumulation.
recommendations.abstractedPrinciple: Always resolve existing test failures before introducing new code changes to maintain system stability.

recommendations.description: Inject a system directive that explicitly prioritizes test remediation over feature expansion when tool outputs indicate failures.
